items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: the band used to play tricks on each other, you know? So, like Posey, he's always posing so much, so we fixed him.

ctx.x: Sam Woodyard still calls him "Piano Red."

(Laughter.) Oh, well, did I tell you that we used to play -- at one time the band used to play tricks on each other, you know? So, like Posey, he's always posing so much, so we fixed him. So we got limburger cheese and cayenne pepper and after we played a dance set he'd get off the stand and leave his horn on the chair, and we stuck the limburger cheese and the cayenne pepper in his mouthpiece because he had a way to lick it before he started playing.
And then, when we got back on the stand and getting ready to play and he'd pick up his horn and he went to lick it and he jumped almost to the ceiling and ran like mad. That was him.

items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: At the time you joined Duke, the 12 members of the band were Johnny Hodges, Barney Bigard, Harry Carney, Arthur Whetsel, Cootie Williams, Freddie Jenkins

ctx.x: No, it was just a new addition, a new funny sound. So, I was soloing from the beginning almost.

At the time you joined Duke, the 12 members of the band were Johnny Hodges, Barney Bigard, Harry Carney, Arthur Whetsel, Cootie Williams, Freddie Jenkins, Joe Nanton, Fred Guy, Wellman Braud, Sonny Greer, and Duke, is that right?
